A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same embedding-norm study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulations, image-representation experiments, confidence analyses, and intervention studies, including additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds regularized simulations, MoCo/DINO comparisons, Adam experiments, Tiny-ImageNet results, and linear-probe evaluations.

M1.justification: Cut-initialization and GradScale retain the same procedures, parameters, and code in Section 6, Listings 1–2, and Algorithm 1. The added experiments apply existing interventions; the explicit temperature notation does not establish a change to the implemented method.

E1.justification: V2 adds Tiny-ImageNet image-classification coverage in Tables 4 and S3. The existing CIFAR, ImageNet-100, Flowers102, human-annotation, synthetic-data, and class-imbalance coverage remains. New optimizers and classifiers change evaluation settings rather than represented tasks.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained SimCLR, SimSiam, and appendix BYOL evaluations, v2 adds default-versus-cut-initialized MoCo V2, MoCo V3, and DINO comparisons on ImageNet-100 in Table 3. This substantially broadens the evaluated method set and introduces a non-cosine-loss comparison.

E3.justification: The standard CIFAR comparison changes from 500 epochs in v1 Table 2 to a reported 1,000 epochs in v2 Table 4; ImageNet-100 remains at 500. New protocols include 100-epoch Adam and MoCo/DINO experiments, top-5 evaluation, linear probing, and regularized simulations. V2's surrounding prose still says 500 epochs, creating an internal inconsistency.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands checks of the proposed explanation: Table 1 tests regularization across initial embedding norms, Tables 6/S4 test robustness under Adam, Table 3 examines MoCo/DINO applicability, and Table S3 checks whether benefits extend beyond kNN evaluation. Earlier batch-size, initialization, imbalance, and opposite-halves analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained confidence and embedding-distribution analyses concern sample properties, not uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results for regularization, Tiny-ImageNet, MoCo/DINO, Adam, and linear probing. CIFAR scores are also replaced under the changed epoch budget: SimCLR's default CIFAR-100 accuracy is 51.9 at 500 epochs in v1 versus 56.6 at 1,000 in v2, not a same-setting gain. The imbalanced results remain identical in v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 5.

T1.justification: Proposition 3.2 and Appendix A.2 add an explicit gradient for a denominator sample and its derivation, replacing the earlier assertions about smaller repulsive gradients and symmetry. Temperature and the unit-temperature assumption become explicit. The principal convergence bound and the proofs in Appendices C and D remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged. The introduction and discussion retain the same central contributions: embedding norms influence convergence, encode confidence, and can be manipulated to improve training. The new evaluations support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 interprets DINO's lack of benefit through its non-cosine objective and argues that the embedding-norm effect persists under Adam. It adds an explanation for collapse under excessive simulated regularization. The shared-weights explanation is narrowed to norm shrinkage rather than also explaining greater non-contrastive sensitivity.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly specifies base learning rates of 0.18 and 0.12 times batch size/256, and k=200 on normalized embeddings. Section 2.1 discloses SimCLR's temperature of 0.5, and Figure S3 clarifies effective-learning-rate calculation. These are additional disclosures; the code link and implementation listings are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Dosovitskiy et al. (2020), Fan et al. (2021), and Le and Yang (2015) alongside the new evaluations. It modestly refines the distinction between prior observations of norm-confidence relationships and explaining them, while preserving the existing related-work framework.

P1.justification: The section and appendix organization largely persists. V2 makes localized prose edits, standardizes kNN terminology, renames Appendix B.1 to Nonparametric Simulations, fixes broken cross-references, and adds an adaptive-optimizer paragraph and Impact Statement. Affiliations, contribution credits, and publication information are updated.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the displayed empirical comparisons through new Tables 1, 3, 6, S3, and S4, and a Tiny-ImageNet column in Table 4. It color-codes the retained initialization sweep and places Algorithm 1 beside Listing 2. Existing figures remain, with limited label, caption, and placement changes.

improvement.justification: The added optimizer, comparator, and linear-probe checks strengthen empirical support beyond v1's original settings, while explicit learning-rate and kNN details improve reproducibility. These are useful incremental gains. Their impact is limited by incomplete protocols for new evaluations and reporting inconsistencies: Table 4 disagrees with the prose on CIFAR epochs, the new simulation objective leaves normalization unclear, and the added Equation 3 has a gradient sign inconsistent with Equation 1.
